add.title: Add a game in seconds. Or a hundred.
add.body: Type a few letters and pick it by its cover. Or paste a whole list, a game on each line, and check the matches. Covers, years and lengths come with every game.

sync.title: Bring your Steam and Switch games with you.
sync.body: Sign in through Steam, and every game you own there lands on your shelf with your hours on it, and each game’s page shows its achievements. Link Nintendo, and the games you played on a Switch or a Switch 2 come too, once you say whether each is a cartridge or a download. Then both keep in step by themselves once a day. Games already on your shelf gain a copy, never a second box. The new ones wait, unsorted, on a page where you rate them and say where each stands, one tap at a time or many at once. PlayStation and Xbox come next.

free.a: Yes. Making a shelf and keeping your games on it costs nothing.

data.q: Where does the information about games come from?
data.a: From IGDB.com: titles, covers, release dates, and how long games take to finish. What is yours you add: where you own a game, how far you got, what you thought of it.

sync.q: Can it bring in the games I already own?
sync.a: From Steam and Nintendo, yes: link them right after signing up, or later on your account page. Every game you own on Steam comes onto your shelf with its hours and achievements; from Nintendo, every game you played on a Switch or a Switch 2, once you say whether each is a cartridge or a download. Both sync again once a day. New games come in unsorted, and one page lets you rate them, give each a status, and put right one taken for the wrong game. PlayStation and Xbox are next. Until then, paste a list of titles, one a line.

who.a: You choose when you sign up, and can change it any time on your account page. A public shelf is for anyone, and search engines can list it; a private one is for you alone. Notes stay private unless you mark them public, game by game, and any one game can be marked private, so only you see it.

export.q: Can I take my games with me?
export.a: Your whole library can be read through Shelf's API while you are signed in. A one-click export is planned.

Sync.title: Platforms
Sync.intro: Bring the games you own on a platform onto your shelf, and keep them in step.

steam.about: Sign in through Steam, and every game you own there goes onto your shelf as a PC copy, with Steam’s hours on it, and its achievements on its page. Shelf syncs again once a day. Your Steam password never reaches Shelf.
steam.public: Steam has to show your game details: open <settings>your Steam privacy settings</settings> (in Steam, Edit Profile, then Privacy Settings) and set Game details to Public.

nintendo.about: Shelf reads the play history Nintendo keeps for your account: every game you have played on a Switch or a Switch 2, with your hours. Nintendo lists what you played, not what you own, so Shelf asks once whether each game is a cartridge or a download. Your Nintendo password never reaches Shelf.
nintendo.how: Nintendo does not send you back to Shelf, so linking takes one copy and paste:
nintendo.again: Sign in on Nintendo’s page again, and paste the new link here:
nintendo.step1: Sign in on Nintendo’s page. It opens in a new tab.
nintendo.step2: When Nintendo shows “Select this account”, do not press it. Copy its link instead: right-click it and choose Copy link address, or on a phone, press and hold it.

outcome.not-the-link: That is not the link from Nintendo’s “Select this account” button. Copy the button’s link, not the page’s address.
outcome.another-sign-in: That link is from another sign-in. Sign in on Nintendo’s page again, and paste the link it gives.
outcome.code-refused: Nintendo did not take that link: each one works once, for a few minutes. Sign in on Nintendo’s page again.
outcome.unset: Nintendo sync isn’t set up on this server yet.
outcome.unreachable: Nintendo did not answer. Try again in a while.

Privacy.metaDescription: What Shelf keeps about you, where, who can see it, and how to remove it.
Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Shelf keeps what it needs to show you your shelf, and nothing to sell. This page says what that is.

account.title: Your account
account.body: Your name, your handle, your email address and a scrambled form of your password, which cannot be turned back into it. Your email address is never shown to anyone.

shelf.title: Your shelf
shelf.body: The games you add and what you say about them: where you own them, how far you got, ratings, dates, tags and notes. A public shelf can be seen by anyone, and search engines can list it; a private one only by you. Notes stay private unless you mark them public, and a game marked private is seen only by you.

signIn.title: Signing in
signIn.body: While you are signed in, a cookie keeps you signed in, and Shelf keeps the address and the browser each session came from, so you can sign out everywhere. A second cookie only says whether you are signed in. Your choices for the shelf, such as the theme, stay in your browser.

steam.title: Steam
steam.body: If you link Steam, Shelf keeps your Steam account’s id and name, and the games Steam lists for it, with the hours played, when each was last played, and what Steam’s store calls each one (a game, a demo, software). For those games, it keeps their achievements as Steam lists them, which of them you unlocked and when, and how many of Steam’s players unlocked each; their artwork is shown from Steam’s own servers. Shelf reads them when you link Steam or press Sync now, and once a day while daily sync is on. Your Steam password never reaches Shelf. Disconnecting Steam deletes what Steam listed; the games it put on your shelf stay, as your own, with their achievements as last read. Linking another Steam account deletes those.

nintendo.title: Nintendo
nintendo.body: If you link Nintendo, Shelf keeps your Nintendo Account’s id and nickname, the games your Nintendo play history lists, with the hours played and when each was last played, and the sign-in Nintendo gives Shelf to read them. That sign-in is kept sealed: what is in the database alone cannot be used. Nintendo’s page names it “Nintendo Store”, as Shelf reads the history that app shows. Shelf reads the history when you link Nintendo or press Sync now, and once a day while daily sync is on. Your Nintendo password never reaches Shelf. Disconnecting Nintendo deletes the sign-in and what Nintendo listed; the games it put on your shelf stay, as your own.

where.title: Where it is kept
where.body: In a database in São Paulo, Brazil (Turso), reached by Shelf’s server, which runs there too (Vercel). The pages of a public shelf are also copied by Vercel’s network around the world so they load quickly. Game information comes from IGDB.com; nothing of yours is sent there. Pressing one of a game's videos plays it in YouTube's player (youtube-nocookie.com), which then sees your visit as YouTube's own pages would; nothing goes to YouTube before you press one.

delete.title: Removing it
delete.body: Delete a game, and it is gone. Delete your account on your account page, and your account, your shelf and everything in it are deleted for good, what Steam and Nintendo listed included.

trademarks.title: Trademarks
trademarks.body: Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Valve Corporation in the U.S. and/or other countries. Nintendo and Nintendo Switch are trademarks of Nintendo. PlayStation is a registered trademark or trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. Xbox is a trademark of the Microsoft group of companies. Shelf names them only to say where your games come from, and is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by any of them.
